messages:
ops-sheriff: :rotating_light: heads up — incidentbot just posted a suppression summary in #incidents, looks like a new filter accidentally muted some pages
incidentbot: [automated] 9 alerts suppressed by rule "exclude_customer_prefix" in paging pipeline (rule introduced in last deploy)
ops-sheriff: when did that deploy go out?
dana: i pushed it at ~15:12 UTC, i thought the rule targeted internal-test tenants only
luis: grabbing notifier-bridge logs now, doing a quick grep
sam: my hunch — regex in the new filter is too permissive, likely a substring match that hits production tenants
maria: do we have any confirmed customer impact?
ops-sheriff: PD shows no new incidents created for those alerts, customers may not have been paged
dana: manually paging the critical cluster via PD UI now, alerting eng-sre on-call list
ops-sheriff: suppressed alert ids from incidentbot: 9867, 9868, 9871, 9872, 9875, 9876, 9880, 9881, 9882
luis: logs excerpt:
```
2026-03-18T15:18:03Z notifier-bridge INFO suppress_rule=exclude_customer_prefix alert_id=9867 matched="redwood-prod-foo"
2026-03-18T15:18:03Z notifier-bridge DEBUG rule_expr="^red-.*$"
```
luis: the rule_expr is wrong — it was supposed to match tenant metadata keys, not raw alert subject
sam: confirmed, commit 1a2b3c introduced the refactor in paging-filter.js that changed the input to the matcher
ops-sheriff: can we flip it back or disable the rule quickly?
dana: i can toggle the suppression flag in the console, doing it now
incidentbot: [automated] suppression flag toggled by dana at 2026-03-18T15:22:10Z
ops-sheriff: once disabled, re-run publishing of suppressed alerts
luis: running republish: `scripts/republish_suppressed --ids 9867,9868,9871,9872,9875,9876,9880,9881,9882`
luis: output: queued 9 alerts for delivery to PagerDuty
pagerduty-bot: 9 incidents created: PD-4421, PD-4422, PD-4423, PD-4424, PD-4425, PD-4426, PD-4427, PD-4428, PD-4429
dana: acked PD-4421 (dana) — oncall responding
maria: customer impact summary: 3 orgs affected (acme, beta-co, redwood-partner); pages delayed ~9 minutes, no escalations seen so far
sam: root cause: naive regex slipped through code review, missing unit test that ensures tenant anchoring
ops-sheriff: immediate action items:
- revert the filter change (sam)
- add unit+integration tests for suppression rules (sam)
- postmortem + customer comms (maria)
- support notify + ticket for affected accounts (maria + dana)
sam: opened PR to revert 1a2b3c (wip), plan to push in ~15m
luis: added a metric and alert: suppression_rate > 5/min with prod/non-prod ratio check
maria: support messaging drafted, will send timeline and remediation steps to affected customers
dana: confirmed manual SMS fallback for top two critical alerts was sent
ops-sheriff: adding this to incident board: severity=P2 (paging automation regression), impact=delayed pages for subset of customers
maria: taking ownership of comms and the postmortem write-up
sam: after revert is merged i'll redeploy to staging, run smoke republish there then one canary in prod
luis: i'll validate no further suppression matches in the last 30m and monitor republished deliveries
ops-sheriff: any remaining manual tasks?
dana: watching PD incidents for ack/escalation; currently stable
incidentbot: [automated] bookkeeping: suppression rule reverted, 9 alerts republished, oncall actions complete
ops-sheriff: thanks everyone :thumbsup: — follow-up postmortem and comms doc will land in #incidents-retros
maria: will file customer follow-ups and loop in success team
sam: adding regression/unit tests to CI and gating deploys on suppression-rule test pass
luis: final check (2026-03-18T15:55Z): suppression matches cleared, no further missed pages reported
